items.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: He was influenced very strongly by Ben Webster and I guess Lester Young.

ctx.x: You know you said that for a time you tried to play like Teddy Wilson. And another great artist, Clark Terry, talked about first imitation, then integration, then innovation.

Well yeah, that’s probably right. I never thought of it that way. That’s right. That’s right. Well you don’t — I don’t think a young person should push themselves to become unique, you just let it happen. Maybe it will never happen I don’t know. But you know I’m thinking of Scott Hamilton. You know when Scott Hamilton first started I started playing with him when he was real young he came to New York. He was influenced very strongly by Ben Webster and I guess Lester Young. And but now, the years have passed and…
People tell me they can identify me now when they hear a record. Well I feel that’s a compliment. That’s kind of nice.
